title: Block: Recursive DFS Over Every Node
oneLiner: Count the connected components of an undirected graph by starting a DFS from every node not yet visited.
keyTakeaway: The outer loop over every node is half the block: each node still unvisited when the loop reaches it starts a new component.
explanation:
There are n nodes, 0 to n - 1, and edges lists undirected edges [a, b]. Return how many connected components there are. Five nodes with edges [0, 1], [1, 2], [3, 4] form 2.

Build an adjacency list, adding each edge in both directions. Write dfs(node): mark it, then call dfs on each unvisited neighbour. Then loop over all nodes; when one is unvisited, count a component and call dfs on it, which marks the whole component.

gotchas: Adding each edge in one direction only, which splits components in an undirected graph.
Forgetting the outer loop, so only the component of node 0 is ever explored.

complexity.note: Every node and edge is handled once; the adjacency list stores every edge twice and the recursion can be V deep.
